title: Minimum Sensors to Cover Grid
summary: Given an n × m grid and an integer k, you are to find the minimum number of sensors needed to cover every cell in the grid.
statement: Given an n × m grid and an integer k, you are to find the minimum number of sensors needed to cover every cell in the grid. Each sensor placed at cell (r, c) will cover all cells within a Chebyshev distance of k from (r, c). The Chebyshev distance between two cells (r1, c1) and (r2, c2) is defined as max(|r1 - r2|, |c1 - c2|).
constraints: The grid dimensions are between one and 1,000.
A sensor covers a square of side at most 2k+1 under Chebyshev distance.
Return the minimum count covering every cell.
hints: Chebyshev coverage is an axis-aligned square spanning at most 2k+1 rows and columns.
Cover each dimension with the minimum number of intervals of that width, then take their Cartesian product.
Each sensor covers at most one width-sized block per dimension, giving the lower bound, and evenly spaced row/column centers attain its product.
editorial: Each sensor covers at most one width-sized block per dimension, giving the lower bound, and evenly spaced row/column centers attain its product.

tests.explanation: Each sensor spans at most three rows and columns, so a two-by-two placement uses four.
One radius-two sensor covers the entire grid.
